candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether limits and reported measurements are expressed as total metal versus another speciation (e.g., dissolved) determines which numeric limit applies and whether a compliance comparison is valid.

candidates.exact_span: It is advised that the influent and effluent samples are collected considering flow detention time through each plant. Analytical MQLs should be used so that the data can also be used for Local Limits assessment and NPDES application purposes.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of 'advised' versus mandatory language affects whether detention-time-based sampling and MQL use are binding monitoring obligations (B). Whether MQL-appropriate data are required for usable results affects how missing or below-MQL values are classified for no-result cases (C).

candidates.exact_span: Maximum Allowable Headworks Loading limitation in ug/l. Only complete for pollutants that have approved Technically Based Local Limits.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The TBLL-approval condition determines which pollutants carry an enforceable headworks loading numeric limit versus an incomplete or non-applicable limit entry, changing which measurements receive a compliance comparison.

candidates.exact_span: Daily average effluent limit in the NPDES permit OR the applicable state Water Quality Standard calculated to an equivalent permit effluent limit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The disjunctive 'OR' requires selecting between the permit-stated daily average limit and a WQS-derived equivalent; different selection yields a different enforceable numeric limit and therefore a different exceedance determination.

candidates.exact_span: Record names of any pollutants [40 CFR 122, Appendix D, Table II and/or Table V] detected and the quantity in which they were detected.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This establishes a reporting obligation for detected Appendix D Table II/V pollutants (B). Whether detection was documented versus absent affects classification of missing-evidence cases and whether a no-result period reflects conditional non-requirement or inadequate evidence (C).
